newsitem.title: UK: Formula One backs adviser Salomon Brothers.
newsitem.headline: Formula One backs adviser Salomon Brothers.

text.p: The legal adviser to Formula One Holdings on Wednesday openly backed the group's financial advisers, Salomon Brothers, amid speculation about the U.S. investment bank's relationship with the UK motor racing group's chief executive.

Stephen Mullens emphasised that the U.S. investment bank was the group's exclusive financial adviser, adding that although any rival plans to the proposed 50 percent flotation were welcome, their merit would judged by Salmon Brothers alone.
"My client has asked me to make clear that Salomon Brothers are the shareholders' exclusive financial adviser and any proposal put forward will be evaluated by Salomon Brothers," Mullens stated.

Speculation has grown that Salomon's rivals have used Formula One as a vehicle with which to attempt to undermine the U.S. investment bank, which has developed a solid position in European equity offerings.

Swiss-owned investment bank SBC Warburg -- which is a member of the syndicate of global managers for the flotation led by Salomon -- has provided independent advice to Formula One's chief executive Bernie Ecclestone.

Amid speculation that the group's expected $2.5-3.3 billion market debut has been delayed or even derailed, Mullens also noted that progress was being made but added that no decision had been made yet on its timing.
Mullens reiterated that an initial public offering was his client's preferred course of action, that plans were on track and promised a statement "in due course".

A company spokesman noted steps were being taken to try and resolve disputes with three key grand prix teams -- Williams, Tyrell and McLaren -- about their revenue share and stake in the floated company.
"I think that progress is being made on this front -- although it will not be resolved until an agreement has been reached," he said.
